issues.description: The docs never describe multi-part assemblies explicitly (returning a dict of parts, part placement in world coordinates, how parameters like fold_angle interact with rotate). I inferred it from the 'return a Part, list or {name: Part}' line.

No way to check clearance across a parameter sweep in one command; I had to rebuild per angle with -p and measure --distance each time. Min distance of arm/forearm is the same at every angle by construction (stacked), so I verified 0 and 120 only.
Docs do not describe assemblies explicitly (returning a list of Parts places them in a shared world frame), nor how to show a parameterised pose; I inferred it from the 'return a list of Parts' line.
No sweep tool: checking clearance across fold angles needed repeated `cad build -p` and `cad measure --distance` runs; renders per angle land in renders/rN with no label of the parameter value.

Docs do not say how to express a parameter-driven rotation of one part inside a multi-part assembly. I had to guess that translate/rotate on a Part mutate in place and that rotate(center=...) or build-at-origin then translate works.

No built-in sweep check over a parameter range. I rebuilt manually at 0/60/90/120 with -p and ran measure --distance each time. Only 4 angles were checked, so clearance at the other angles is argued from the stacking, not measured.
Renders are per revision directory (renders/rN), so the renders for different fold angles end up in separate revision folders. No option to name or label them with the parameter value.

Docs say hole_pattern 'centres the grid' about center=(0,0) with the example using a plate centred at origin; it wasn't explicit whether center is absolute world XY (it is, as verified via inspect) so I had to verify for a corner-origin plate.

hole_pattern's center is in plate coordinates only via a one-line note ('centres the grid ... (±24, ±14)'); it was not obvious that center= is an absolute XY position, which matters for plates with a corner at the origin. Confirmed by inspect.

Docs do not describe assemblies/multi-part output beyond 'return a list of Parts'; had to guess that a Parameter-driven rotate() on one part works as the articulation, and that rotate about Y needs a negative angle to swing -Z toward +X (right-hand rule, derived by reasoning, then verified through find_holes).
No built-in all-pairs clearance check across parts or sweep over a parameter; I verified clearance by reasoning (links sit in separate Y layers) plus one distance measure at 90 deg.

The rotate() sign convention for Part.rotate about Y vs. the task's 'positive angle swings foot toward +X' needed a numeric check; I had to negate the angle (-knee_angle). Verified via find_holes at 90 deg (foot at x=110).

No built-in sweep/min-distance check across a parameter range; I had to rebuild with -p at several angles and call measure --distance manually. Clearance is guaranteed here by Y layering, not by a sweep.
XZ plane extrudes toward -Y and offset=d places the sketch at Y=-d, so placing a slab at a given Y range (e.g. Y 0..5.5) requires offset=-ymax and positive distance; counter-intuitive.
cad measure --holes output has no explicit angle-sorted/flat format; also measure --distance prints full part info each time (noisy).

Rotation sign for rotate(angle, axis='y') is easy to get wrong: positive angle sends -Z toward -X, so knee_angle needed rotate(-knee_angle). Docs state the right-hand rule but a worked example for 'swing a hanging link toward +X' would help. I verified it via find_holes positions.

Not stated whether Profile.slot length is overall or center-to-center (it is overall, found by checking bbox). Also the XZ plane extrusion direction (-Y) plus offset sign (offset=-ymid puts mid-plane at Y=ymid) takes care to get right.

No built-in multi-part clearance or sweep check across parameter values. I ran cad set + cad measure --distance manually at 0, 45 and 90 degrees. Only the distance between parts is reported, not a pairwise matrix.

There is no hole-along-Y-through-everything helper that takes a 2D position on a part with several features. I cut cylinders with op='cut' on axis y instead. cad set leaves params.toml behind, so I ran cad unset to restore the default angle.
Multi-part assemblies have no placement or joint concept. The rotation of the lower link is baked into the part geometry, so its part coordinates change with the parameter.

No way to declare the sensor envelope as a keep-out/reference solid and have inspect report interference/contact/clearance against it; I relied on cutting an envelope cylinder and did not run a numeric contact check or view a section render.
Hole positions given as 2D (x,y) worked fine; no problems with the build.

No way to declare the sensor envelope as a reference body and check keep-out/contact/clearance from the CLI; I verified by reasoning about the geometry (cut cylinder R15 at Z=25 gives exact tangent contact). I did not open the renders in detail.

No way to declare the sensor envelope / keep-out volumes and check clearance or touching in the CLI; I verified by reasoning and one render. I did not try building envelope Parts for distance_to/interference.
find_holes reports the sensor-seat cylindrical cut as a 'hole' d=30, which is noise when looking for screw holes.
Shell redirection/heredoc file creation was blocked by the harness approval; had to use the Write tool. Not a cad issue.

No built-in way to check a requirement like 'clear vertical column above a point' or 'min clearance from an envelope box'; I verified by reasoning from dimensions rather than a query. Envelope boxes would need to be built as helper Parts to use distance_to.
Compound shell commands (heredocs followed by several cad calls) were blocked by the sandbox approval, so I had to write files with the Write tool. This is environment friction, not a cad bug.
I did not run cad measure --distance between the parts and the servo envelope, and I did not run any clearance or keepout check. The envelope is not a model object, so I checked the numbers by hand.
No way to import/declare the servo envelope as a reference body, so clearance (>=0.5 mm) and contact checks against it were done by hand arithmetic rather than with distance_to/interference.
Hex pocket orientation (flats parallel to X) had to be inferred from the regular_polygon note (angle=0 -> flats at v=±AF/2); I did not verify it numerically, only in a section render.
No obvious CLI to measure the interference/distance between two parts of the same project in one command; I relied on construction (touching at Z=0) instead.
Hex orientation: had to infer that regular_polygon angle=0 (corner on +u) gives flats parallel to X; docs say flats at v=±af, which was enough but needed a moment of thought.
cylinder(axis='x', align=...) semantics for where 'at' sits along the axis were only briefly described; used align='min' starting beyond the part and a long length.
find_holes/inspect does not report the half-bore (open half-cylinder) as a hole, so the 8.2 mm bore could only be verified visually via section render.
Cylinder 'align' semantics for axis='x' with at= were inferred (align='min' starts at the 'at' point along the axis); worked but not shown in an example.

suggestions.suggestion: Add 'cad sweep fold_angle=0:120:30 --measure-distance a,b' for assembly clearance checks.
Document assembly conventions and that renders are stored per revision (so different angles need different builds).
Add an assembly/motion docs section with an example sweeping a parameter and checking min distance.
Include parameter values in render folder names or metadata.
Let `cad measure --distance` print only a summary rather than the full part report.
Add an assembly section to the docs showing a posed/articulated multi-part example.
Add `cad sweep fold_angle 0:120:10 --distance a b` or similar for pairwise clearance over a parameter range.
Include parameter values in render filenames or the directory name.
State explicitly that hole_pattern center is in world coordinates, and show an example with a corner-origin box.
Document that hole_pattern center is in absolute plate coordinates (not relative to the part) with an example for corner-origin plates.
Add a docs example of hole_pattern on a corner-origin plate with center=(w/2, h/2).
Offer a center='part' option for hole_pattern.
Add a 'cad check clearance' for all part pairs, optionally sweeping a parameter range.
Document the Profile.slot angle semantics and that 'length' is overall end-to-end.
Allow render to take -p knee_angle=45 without rewriting params.toml.
Add a box-with-Y-range helper or an extrude option taking absolute start/end coordinates along the normal.
Add `cad measure A --distance B -p knee_angle=0:90:15` sweep support.
Document that rotate on a returned Part list member mutates in place and how assemblies use parameters for motion.
Add an assembly example, such as a hinge or linkage, that uses a rotating parameter and separate parts.
Add a cad check or measure --all-pairs command that prints the pairwise distance matrix and can sweep a parameter over a range.
State in the docs whether Profile.slot length is overall, and add a pivot-aware rotate example.
Render all parts in one image at several parameter values with one command, for example render -p knee_angle=0,45,90.
Allow named keep-out solids in cad.toml checked by inspect (interference, contact distance, vertical-path clearance for screw heads).
Allow non-part 'envelope' bodies for distance/interference checks and render overlays.
Allow a keepout/envelope declaration in the project that cad inspect checks automatically.
Let find_holes filter by through/vertical or diameter.
Add a way to declare keep-out/envelope volumes in the project and check clearance/interference against them via cad measure.
A 'cad check' for min wall thickness would be useful.
Let a project declare reference or envelope solids that are excluded from export but available to measure --distance and interference.
Add a helper that reports the minimum wall thickness around holes.
Allow declaring non-exported 'envelope' parts for distance/interference checks and rendering.
Add a column-clearance query (is a vertical cylinder of D at (x,y) free of all parts).
Add a worked example for split/two-part assemblies with hex nut pockets.
inspect could report hex pocket (non-circular recess) dimensions and flat orientation.
Add a worked example for a split/two-part assembly with a bore and nut pockets.
Let hole() take a 'name' collision-free pattern; names with negative numbers like screw_t-10 are ugly.
Report partial/open cylindrical cuts (half bores) in find_holes or a separate 'cylindrical cuts' list.
Add a hex-pocket / nut-trap helper or doc example showing regular_polygon across_flats orientation relative to a given axis.
